Plugin Ecosystem

Built-in Plugins

Extensibility

Plugins API

Extend Flutcom's capabilities globally. Write vanilla JavaScript logic once, and use it across every view, component, and route without ever redefining functions.

A Flutcom plugin is just a .js file that exposes a global API via window. No class boilerplate. No build step. Pure JavaScript.

Zero Overhead

Loaded once at boot. No re-evaluation on navigation.

Globally Available

Call your plugin from any view with window.MyPlugin.method().

Framework-Agnostic

Any existing vanilla JS library can become a plugin in minutes.

Creating a Plugin

Two simple steps to register any plugin in Flutcom.

1

Register in Config

Add your plugin file to the resources array in flutcom.config.js.

// flutcom.config.js
export const resources = [
  { type: "js", file: "plugins/my-plugin.js" }
];
2

Write the Plugin

Expose your logic as a global object on window.

// plugins/my-plugin.js
(function () {
  window.MyPlugin = {
    greet: (name) =>
      `Hello, ${name}!`
  };
})();

Then call it from any view:

resources/views/home.html
<!-- Inline script inside any view -->
<script>
  const msg = window.MyPlugin.greet('Flutcom');
  console.log(msg); // "Hello, Flutcom!"
</script>

Lifecycle Hooks

Because Flutcom is a hash-router SPA, the page never fully reloads. You can hook into navigation events to run code on every route change.

plugins/page-tracker.js 
(function () {

  function onRouteChange() {
    const route = location.hash || '#home';
    console.log(`[Router] Navigated to: ${route}`);
    // Update page title dynamically
    document.title = `Flutcom — ${route.replace('#', '')}`;
  }

  // Fires on every SPA navigation
  window.addEventListener('hashchange', onRouteChange);

  // Also fires on initial page load
  window.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', onRouteChange);

})();

Pro Tip — Persistent Event Listeners

Because Flutcom never reloads the page, event listeners registered in a plugin will persist across all routes without duplicating. This is ideal for analytics, scroll trackers, and global shortcuts.

Global Store Plugin

Flutcom ships with a reactive store plugin for sharing state between views without prop-drilling.

plugins/store.js (usage) 
// Set a value from any view or component
window.FlutStore.set('user', { name: 'Alex', role: 'admin' });

// Get a value from any other view
const user = window.FlutStore.get('user');
console.log(user.name); // "Alex"

// Subscribe to changes reactively
window.FlutStore.subscribe('user', (newValue) => {
  document.getElementById('username').textContent = newValue.name;
});

// Clear the store on logout
window.FlutStore.clear();
.set(key, value)

Store any value globally. Notifies all subscribers.

.get(key)

Retrieve a stored value from any view or script.

.subscribe(key, fn)

React to state changes in real-time, like a watcher.

Example: Customer Analytics

A real-world plugin that tracks user behavior and manages customer session data across your entire SPA automatically.

plugins/customer-tracker.js
(function () {

  window.CustomerTracker = {

    trackPageView: function(viewName) {
      console.log(`[Analytics] Visited: ${viewName}`);
      // Send to your backend or Google Analytics here
      fetch('/api/analytics', {
        method: 'POST',
        body: JSON.stringify({ page: viewName, ts: Date.now() })
      });
    },

    getUserSession: function() {
      return JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('customer_session')) || {};
    },

    setSession: function(data) {
      localStorage.setItem('customer_session', JSON.stringify(data));
    }
  };

  // Automatically track every SPA navigation
  window.addEventListener('hashchange', () => {
    window.CustomerTracker.trackPageView(location.hash);
  });

})();

Built-in: Copy to Clipboard

Flutcom ships with a clipboard plugin that automatically adds copy functionality to any element with a data-copy attribute.

HTML Usage
<!-- Add data-copy to any button -->
<button data-copy="npm create flutcom@latest">
  Copy Command
</button>

<!-- Works on any element -->
<code data-copy="some text to copy">Click to copy</code>

The plugin is already registered in flutcom.config.js by default. It listens for click events on elements with data-copy and automatically writes the value to the clipboard. No extra code needed.

Built-in: Native Modals

Flutcom ships with an async modal plugin. It fetches HTML from resources/modals/ and injects it into the DOM with smooth entrance animations.

Usage 
// Open a modal by name (loads resources/modals/modal-login.html)
window.flutcomModals.open('modal-login');

// Use the returned object to close it programmatically
const { close } = await window.flutcomModals.open('modal-confirm');
setTimeout(close, 5000); // Auto-close after 5s

// Trigger from any HTML button
<button onclick="flutcomModals.open('modal-deploy')">Deploy</button>

Modal File Structure

resources/modals/modal-confirm.html
<div data-modal-overlay class="fixed inset-0 z-[100] bg-black/80 flex items-center justify-center">
  <div class="modal-container bg-zinc-900 rounded-2xl p-8 max-w-md">
    <button data-modal-close>✕</button>
    <h2>Are you sure?</h2>
    <p>This action cannot be undone.</p>
  </div>
</div>

Best Practices

Always use an IIFE

Wrap your plugin in an Immediately Invoked Function Expression (function(){})() to avoid polluting the global scope beyond your intentional exports.

Name your plugins clearly

Use descriptive PascalCase names like window.AuthPlugin or window.ToastPlugin to avoid collisions with browser APIs or third-party scripts.

Don't re-register listeners on navigation

Since Flutcom is a SPA, your plugin's event listeners persist automatically. Avoid adding them inside view-level scripts which run on every navigation — register them once inside the plugin file.
